Alexander Berkman, The Bolshevik Myth.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/alexander-berkman/the-bolshevik-myth

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Alexander Berkman, author, died 1936 (Wikidata Q195390, death 1936-06-28).

First publication of the text used: January 1925, published by Boni and Liveright (Wikipedia, The Bolshevik Myth: 'it was published in January 1925'). Boni & Liveright has its headquarters in New York City (Wikipedia, Boni & Liveright). SE colophon: 'The Bolshevik Myth was published in 1925 by Alexander Berkman.'

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1925, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (United States): the publisher is headquartered in New York, so the country of first publication is taken as the United States. The text was first published there before 1931, so the US rule settles the origin too, whatever Berkman's death year.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
